text:
marta: putting a short proposal on the table: set Action SLOs for postmortem items so owners have clear expectations and we can measure velocity. want lightweight defaults + a tiny automation called 'owner-pingback'. quick sketch below.

ken: sounds useful. what are the SLO tiers?

marta: default tiers: SLO-1 = 72h (code/patch), SLO-2 = 7d (config/ops), SLO-3 = 14d (procurement/infra). owners can pick, product can override with justification.

lucy: +1. propose we require: owner, verifier, one-line acceptance criteria, evidence link. also add an "owner-pingback" that DM's the owner at T+24h if no update. keeps things moving without noisy channels.

rahul: automation idea: on postmortem publish, create compact tracker items with the following template (one-line fields) so it's easy to scan and auto-sort by SLO:```
Action SLO row:
- Owner: <name>
- SLO: SLO-1|SLO-2|SLO-3
- Due: <date or tier>
- Verifier: <name>
- One-line acceptance: <what "done" looks like>
- Evidence: <metric link/canary>
- Blocker reason (if slipped): <short text>
- Tags: <recurrence-signal>
```

marta: love the evidence requirement. too many closures say "looks ok". require a metric graph or canary link for verification.

ken: also add a tiny rollback plan field. if the change causes regression we want a known revert. one line.

lucy: process: publish pm -> bot creates rows -> owners get DM ping at T+24h -> if no update by T+72h escalate to shadow owner and add a short unblock note. summaries posted weekly to product leads with counts by recurrence-tag.

oncall-bot: automated: created SLO items SLO-31456 and SLO-31457 for incident 3145678901, assigned to @marta and @ken. reminders: T+24h DM, T+72h escalation. links: https://tracker.example/SLO-31456, https://tracker.example/SLO-31457

rahul: metrics idea: track median time-to-close per SLO tier and percent closed within SLO. put a small widget on the incident dashboard. can surface regressions as "percent over SLO" by recurrence tag.

marta: governance: run a monthly "velocity review" where we scan items that breached SLOs and capture root cause for breach (procurement, unclear owner, infra risk). put those notes back into the postmortem as a short addendum.

ken: tiny comms template for execs: 2 lines: 1) Highest-risk open action + SLO, 2) next checkpoint + owner. terse.
lucy: agree. also recommend a short "why this slipped" checkbox when closing late to build the recurrence heatmap.

marta: next steps: 1) rahul to add tracker template and widgets this week, 2) lucy to spec the owner-pingback DM wording, 3) ken to draft the rollback one-liner guidance. i'll run a two-week pilot on current open postmortems.

ken: ping me if you want a hand populating the pilot.

marta: thanks all  will push the template to /incidents/process and tag the pilot. if anyone has edits, drop them here or open a tiny PR. :rocket:
